absaetze.t: Combien dépensent les Espagnols, les Allemands ou les Belges pour faire le plein d'essence ou de diesel à la pompe ? En moyenne, un Européen doit débourser 1,93 euros pour un litre d'essence (sans plomb 95) et 2,15 euros pour un litre de diesel selon les dernières données de la Commission européenne. Mais cette moyenne cache des disparités parfois importantes entre États membres.
Les prix de l'essence SP95 et du gazole dans chaque pays

Les données publiées par la Commission européenne correspondent à une moyenne nationale pour chaque pays, selon le bulletin publié le 5 novembre 2026 et sur la base de prix relevés au 2 novembre. À cette date, le litre d'essence sans plomb 95 (SP95) dépasse les 2 euros dans huit pays de l'UE : au Danemark (2,50 euros), aux Pays-Bas (2,28 euros), en Finlande (2,21 euros), en France (2,16 euros), en Allemagne (2,13 euros), en Grèce (2,13 euros), au Portugal (2,01 euros) et en Italie (2,00 euros).

Pour le litre du gazole, son prix dépasse désormais les 2 euros dans dix-neuf pays, soit dans plus de deux tiers des États membres. Son plus haut niveau est atteint au Danemark (2,53 euros), aux Pays-Bas (2,47 euros) et en Finlande (2,43 euros).

Les Français doivent débourser en moyenne 2,16 euros pour un litre d'essence (SP95) et 2,37 euros pour un litre de gazole, ce qui place respectivement la France à la quatrième place et à la cinquième place des pays avec les prix les plus élevés de l'UE.

À l'inverse, c'est à Malte que l'essence est la moins chère : 1,34 euro le litre. C'est aussi dans ce pays que le prix du diesel défie toute concurrence dans l'UE : 1,21 euro le litre. Cette situation est le fruit d'une politique de prix fixes lancée par l'État qui absorbe l'inflation via des subventions. Cette politique de prix bas coûte toutefois de plus en plus cher aux finances publiques maltaises. L'archipel affiche, de loin, les tarifs les plus bas. Aucun autre pays ne se situe au-dessous de 1,4 euro pour un litre d'essence ou de 1,8 euro pour un litre de gazole.
Une hausse brutale depuis les attaques contre l'Iran

Depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en Iran le 28 février 2026, la hausse des prix du carburant est brutale. Cette flambée s'explique par les craintes sur l'approvisionnement mondial, les perturbations du trafic dans le détroit d'Ormuz et la tension particulière sur les produits raffinés, notamment le diesel et le kérosène, dont l'Europe dépend en partie du Moyen-Orient.

Avant cela, la première grande phase de hausse visible du XXIe siècle remonte aux années 2005-2008, avec une montée presque continue jusqu'au pic de l’été 2008 : le litre de SP95 est passé d'un peu plus de 1,04 euro début janvier 2005 à environ 1,47 euro début juillet 2008. Cette poussée s'inscrit dans le grand cycle mondial de hausse du pétrole de l'époque, porté par une demande très forte, notamment dans les économies émergentes, alors que la production mondiale stagnait davantage. Après ce pic, la crise financière mondiale a provoqué un retournement brutal, avec une rechute des prix en 2008-2009.

Une deuxième grande séquence haussière est ensuite apparue en 2009-2012, puis une troisième en 2021-2022. Après le creux du début 2009, le SP95 est remonté jusqu'à 1,69 euro au printemps 2012, dans un contexte de reprise économique et de tensions d'offre liées notamment à la guerre civile en Libye et aux sanctions contre l'Iran. Plus récemment, après le point bas exceptionnel du Covid (1,16 euro le litre le 4 mai 2020), les prix ont rebondi avec la reprise post-pandémie en 2021, avant de bondir de nouveau en 2022 avec la guerre en Ukraine et la crise énergétique européenne. Mais l'Agence internationale de l'énergie rappelle que les marchés avaient commencé à se tendre dès 2021, avant l'aggravation provoquée par l'invasion russe.
Les taxes sur les carburants diffèrent selon les pays

Pourquoi ces différences de prix de l'essence et du diesel entre États membres de l'UE existent-elles ? Le prix à la pompe est fixé par chaque distributeur en fonction de quatre paramètres principaux : le coût du pétrole et de son raffinage, le coût de son transport, la marge du distributeur et enfin les taxes nationales. Chaque paramètre influe sur la différence des prix à la pompe entre les distributeurs et entre les pays.
Les carburants sont taxés à deux principaux niveaux :
le droit d'accise : un prélèvement fixe par litre qui n'augmente pas automatiquement avec le prix du pétrole. Certains pays imposent aussi des taxes carbone ou d'autres prélèvements.

la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) : elle est calculée sur le prix du carburant une fois les droits d'accise et autres prélèvements éventuels ajoutés. Les automobilistes paient donc de la TVA sur les droits d'accise (un impôt sur l'impôt).
Le droit d'accise

Sur les droits d'accise, l'Union européenne exige que les États membres prélèvent un droit minimum de 0,36 € par litre d'essence sans plomb et de 0,33 € par litre de diesel. Mais la fiscalité appliquée aux carburants comporte des écarts importants selon les États membres, d'après les données de la Commission.

A la date du 2 novembre 2026, les Pays-Bas, la Finlande, le Danemark, la Grèce et la France sont les pays appliquant les droits d'accise les plus élevés sur l'essence. S'agissant de l'accise sur le gazole, le classement est différent. Arrive en tête l'Italie, suivie de la France, la Belgique, du Danemark et des Pays-Bas.

La France applique en 2026 un droit d'accise de 0,69 euro par litre d'essence et de 0,61 euro par litre de gazole. Elle se situe ainsi, parmi les Vingt-Sept, à la cinquième place pour l'essence et à la deuxième pour le diesel. La moyenne de l'UE se situant à 0,51 euro le litre pour l'essence et 0,39 euro le litre pour le gazole.
La TVA

En vertu d'une directive de l'UE, la TVA ne peut pas être inférieure à 15 %. Là encore, le taux diffère entre les pays. La Hongrie applique une TVA de 27 % sur les carburants (le taux est le même sur l'essence et le gazole), quand le Luxembourg applique un taux de 17 %. La moyenne européenne est à 21,4 %. La France à 20 % se situe donc en-dessous.
Quels pays taxent le plus ?

En prenant en compte l'ensemble des taxes - accise, TVA et éventuelles taxes supplémentaires, les pays taxant le plus l'essence au 2 novembre 2026 sont les Pays-Bas, le Danemark, la Finlande, la Grèce et la France. Pour ces cinq pays, les taxes représentent entre 55 % et 49 % du prix total de l'essence.
S'agissant de gazole, arrivent en tête le Danemark, l'Italie, la Belgique, la Finlande et la France. Dans ces États, les taxes représentent entre 41 % et 46 % du prix total du gazole.
Pour les deux types de carburants, la France arrive en cinquième position des pays de l'UE taxant le plus, les taxes représentant 49 % du prix total de l'essence et 42 % du prix total du gazole.
Pourquoi en France le prix du gazole augmente-t-il plus vite que celui de l'essence ?

Le droit d'accise sur l'essence est plus élevé que celui sur le gazole, ce qui explique que, hors période de crise, le sans plomb est légèrement plus cher que le diesel. Mais si depuis le déclenchement de la guerre au Moyen-Orient, le 28 février dernier, le prix du gazole a parfois dépassé celui de l'essence, c'est en raison de la loi de l'offre et de la demande. Quand la demande dépasse l'offre, les prix augmentent. Et le diesel est davantage utilisé que le sans plomb, puisqu'il alimente encore la moitié du parc automobile français. D'après l'Insee, en 2024, la consommation de diesel en France a atteint 28 millions de tonnes, contre 11,1 millions pour l'essence (ce chiffre comprend le sans plomb 95 et 98, y compris le superéthanol E85).

items.titel: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
items.anriss: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

absaetze.t: Speaking to Spanish, Portuguese and Latin American leaders, he appealed for transformers, power cables, generators and electronic equipment to restore infrastructure damaged by Russian attacks. Zelensky specifically identified Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Colombia as potential suppliers of transformers, Chile for power cables and Spain for electrical equipment and generators. He stressed that Ukraine needed supplies compatible with its electricity grid and urged governments to establish direct contacts with manufacturers to accelerate deliveries.
ADVERTISEMENT

At the summit, Zelensky was seen speaking with UN Secretary-General António Guterres and attending talks alongside Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, Honduran President Nasry Asfura and other international leaders.
The Ukrainian leader also met Spain's King Felipe VI at the Zarzuela Palace, where he was welcomed alongside Spanish Defence Minister Margarita Robles.

His appeal placed Ukraine's energy needs at the centre of discussions, highlighting the importance of cooperation beyond Europe as Russian strikes continue to damage essential infrastructure. Zelensky emphasised that restoring the power network required not only international support but also rapid access to specialised equipment.

items.titel: Hunderttausende protestieren in Frankreich für bessere Lebensbedingungen
items.anriss: Der Ruf nach höheren Löhnen, Steuergerechtigkeit und mehr Geld für Bildung hat in Frankreich erneut Hunderttausende auf die Straßen getrieben. Der Aktionstag verlief weitgehend friedlich, es kam mancherorts dennoch zu Ausschreitungen.[ …

absaetze.t: Schüler, Gelbwesten und Gewerkschaften Unzufriedenheit treibt erneut Hunderttausende auf die Straßen

Der Ruf nach höheren Löhnen, Steuergerechtigkeit und mehr Geld für Bildung hat in Frankreich erneut Hunderttausende auf die Straßen getrieben. Der Aktionstag verlief weitgehend friedlich, es kam mancherorts dennoch zu Ausschreitungen.

In Frankreich sind nach Angaben des Innenministeriums erneut Hunderttausende Menschen landesweit auf die Straßen gegangen, um bessere Bedingungen an Schulen und Universitäten und höhere Gehälter zu fordern. Nach Angaben des Innenministeriums waren 575.000 Menschen auf der Straße. Der Gewerkschaftsbund CGT sprach von fast 1,6 Millionen Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmern bei mehr als 200 Demonstrationen. Damit handelt es sich auf jeden Fall um die bislang größten Kundgebungen in Frankreich in diesem Herbst. Zudem gab es einen Streik im öffentlichen Dienst. Etwa zehn Prozent der Beschäftigten dort legten die Arbeit nieder.
Erneute Ausschreitungen und Festnahmen

Überschattet wurden die Massenproteste allerdings erneut von Angriffen auf Einsatzkräfte und Brandstiftungen. In zahlreichen Großstädten wie Rennes, Marseille, Nantes, Lyon, Bordeaux und Straßburg hätten Gruppen von jeweils mehreren Hundert radikalen Kräften und Linksextremisten Polizisten mit Wurfgeschossen und Feuerwerkskörpern angegriffen und versucht, aus den Demonstrationszügen auszubrechen und in die Stadtzentren vorzudringen, teilte das Innenministerium am Abend mit. Gewalt wurde auch aus Paris gemeldet.

Landesweit gab es nach einer vorläufigen Bilanz 448 Festnahmen, 53 Polizeibeamte wurden verletzt und es gab 86 Brandstiftungen. Beamte wurden unter anderem mit Steinen, Boule-Kugeln und improvisierten Sprengsätzen beworfen. Schwere Sachbeschädigungen und Gewalt gab es an etlichen Schulen in Frankreich. Schulpersonal wurde in einigen Städten mit Feuerwerkskörpern beschossen und verletzt.

Im Pariser Vorort La Courneuve stach ein junger Mann mit einem Messer auf einen Schüler ein, der an der Blockade einer Schule beteiligt war. In Toulouse drangen Randalierer in eine Schule ein und legten einen Brand, verwüsteten Räume und zerstörten Computer.
Zehntausende Polizisten im Einsatz

In Paris blieb der Eiffelturm wegen des Streiks geschlossen. Zahlreiche Regionalzüge fielen aus. In mehreren Fällen hatten die Behörden Kundgebungen in den Innenstädten verboten, um Plünderungen von Geschäften zu verhindern. Nach Angaben von Innenminister Laurent Nuñez waren landesweit 70.000 Polizisten im Einsatz, unterstützt von Panzerfahrzeugen, Drohnen und Hubschraubern.
An den vergangenen Wochenenden waren bei Ausschreitungen am Rande der Proteste rund 3.000 Geschäfte beschädigt und geplündert worden.
"Wir brauchen konkrete Antworten"

Der Aktionstag war ein weiterer Teil der Protestwelle, die seit fast zwei Monaten durchs Land rollt. Mehrere Gewerkschaften hatten schon Anfang Oktober dazu aufgerufen. Schüler- und Studierendenverbände sowie die Gelbwesten-Bewegung unterstützten den Aufruf und sorgten damit für höhere Teilnehmerzahlen. Diejenigen, die friedlich protestieren, sprechen von einer "convergence des colères", einer "Vereinigung der Wut".

Marylise Léon, die Chefin der Gewerkschaft CFDT, sagte: "Wir wollen eine klare Botschaft an die Regierung senden, dass wir konkrete Lösungen brauchen, die auf die Schwierigkeiten der Arbeitnehmer eingehen, am Ende des Monats über die Runden zu kommen. Die Kaufkraft ist seit Monaten ein Thema. Wir brauchen konkrete Antworten!"
Blockaden vor Schulen im ganzen Land

Am Morgen hatten Schülerinnen und Schüler erneut Blockaden aus Mülltonnen und Absperrgittern vor zahlreichen Schulen errichtet. Nach Gewerkschaftsangaben waren landesweit knapp 1.000 der insgesamt 3.700 Oberschulen von Blockaden betroffen. Die Regierung meldete 81 blockierte Schulen und 16 Prozent Streikbeteiligung bei den Lehrkräften. Auch jede dritte Hochschule war von Protestaktionen betroffen.

"Ich bin Lehrerin und hier, um unseren öffentlichen Dienst zu verteidigen. Um den Jugendlichen zu sagen, dass sie ein Recht auf Bildung und eine Zukunft haben", sagte eine Demonstrationsteilnehmerin in Paris. "Wir sind hier als Eltern, aber auch als Bürger. Uns blutet das Herz beim Gedanken an unsere Republik."

Frankreichs Oberstufenschüler protestieren seit Mitte September gegen Lehrermangel, zu lange Schultage, Schulgebäude in marodem Zustand und die undurchsichtige Vergabe von Studienplätzen. Die Regierung versprach ein neues Bewerbungsverfahren und mehr Lehrerstellen, was die Schülerverbände jedoch als unzureichend bezeichneten.
Regierung plant "Sozialkonferenz"

Die Proteste gelten als erneute Herausforderung für Präsident Emmanuel Macron und die Regierung. Sie finden rund fünf Monate vor der Präsidentschaftswahl statt, bei der Macron nach seiner zweiten Amtszeit nicht wieder antreten darf.
Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu kündigte für Montag eine "Sozialkonferenz" an, um auf die Forderungen der Demonstranten einzugehen.
Mit Informationen von Carolin Dylla, ARD Paris

items.titel: Hunderttausende demonstrieren friedlich – doch auch wieder Gewalt
items.anriss: Hunderttausende Menschen haben in Frankreich für höhere Gehälter und eine Anhebung des Mindestlohns demonstriert.

absaetze.t: Hunderttausende Menschen haben in Frankreich an einem nationalen Streik- und Protesttag der Gewerkschaften für höhere Gehälter und eine Anhebung des Mindestlohns demonstriert.
Landesweit seien es mehr als 600'000 Personen gewesen, teilte das Innenministerium mit. Der Gewerkschaftsbund CGT sprach von knapp 1.6 Millionen Teilnehmern.
Überschattet wurden die Massenproteste allerdings erneut von Angriffen auf Einsatzkräfte und Brandstiftungen.
In Paris schlug die zunächst friedliche Stimmung um, als einige Demonstranten mit der Polizei aneinandergerieten, die daraufhin Tränengas einsetzte.

In zahlreichen weiteren Grossstädten wie Rennes, Marseille, Nantes, Lyon, Bordeaux und Strassburg hätten Gruppen von jeweils mehreren hundert radikalen Kräften und Linksextremisten Polizisten mit Wurfgeschossen und Feuerwerkskörpern angegriffen. Sie versuchten zudem, aus den Demonstrationszüge auszubrechen und in die Stadtzentren vorzudringen, teilte das Innenministerium mit.

Landesweit gab es nach einer vorläufigen Bilanz 448 Festnahmen, 53 Polizeibeamte wurden verletzt und es gab 86 Brandstiftungen. Beamte wurden unter anderem mit Steinen, Boule-Kugeln und improvisierten Sprengsätzen beworfen. In Strassburg wurde eine offenbar von Kunststudenten entworfene Puppe, die einen Bereitschaftspolizisten abbilden sollte, in Brand gesetzt. Der Präfekt habe die Justiz eingeschaltet, hiess es aus dem Ministerium.
Zahlreiche Schulen beschädigt

Schwere Sachbeschädigungen und Gewalt gab es an etlichen Schulen in Frankreich, wie das Ministerium mitteilte. Schulpersonal wurde in einigen Städten mit Feuerwerkskörpern beschossen und verletzt. Im Pariser Vorort La Courneuve verpasste ein junger Mann einem Schüler einen Messerstich, der an der Blockade einer Schule beteiligt war.

In Toulouse drangen Randalierer in eine Schule ein und legten einen Brand, verwüsteten Räume und zerstörten Computer. In Caen wurden zwei Gymnasien schwer beschädigt. In Lille wurde der Eingang eines Gymnasiums in Brand gesetzt, wonach die Schule evakuiert werden musste.
Anschluss an die Protestbewegung

Zum Protesttag hatten die Gewerkschaften aufgerufen. An den frankreichweit bislang grössten Demonstrationen beteiligten sich nach letzten Angaben des Innenministeriums 575'000 Menschen, davon 65'000 in Paris. Der Gewerkschaftsbund CGT sprach am Abend von 1.6 Millionen Teilnehmern landesweit.

Mit den Gewerkschafts­demonstrationen setzen sich die seit Wochen andauernden Sozialproteste in Frankreich fort, die bislang federführend von Schüler- und Studentenorganisationen und der Gelbwestenbewegung organisiert wurden. Bei diesen Massenprotesten ging es vor allem um eine bessere Ausstattung von Schulen, um Polizeigewalt und die zu hohen Lebenshaltungskosten.
Premier kündigt Sozialkonferenz an

In Reaktion auf die Massenproteste kündigte Premierminister Sébastien Lecornu für Montag eine Sozialkonferenz mit Arbeitnehmer- und Arbeitgeberverbänden an, «um Lösungen für Fragen der Kaufkraft und der Löhne zu finden». Der Arbeitsminister solle seine Konsultationen in der Sache bis Sonntag abschliessen. Parallel dazu setze der Minister für öffentliche Finanzen seinen Dialog mit den Vertretern des öffentlichen Dienstes fort.

«Die Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer erleben einen beispiellosen sozialen Abstieg. Kraftstoff, Lebensmittel, Mieten, Gas, Strom … alles wird teurer, nur die Löhne und Renten steigen nicht», hiess es in einer gemeinsamen Erklärung der Gewerkschaften. Diese warnten die Regierung und die Arbeitgeber: «Die Wut ist gross. Die Lage des Landes ist prekär. Auf die dringenden sozialen und ökologischen Probleme muss unverzüglich reagiert werden.»
Eine Erhöhung des Mindestlohns um 100 Euro netto pro Monat forderte die Chefin der Gewerkschaft CFDT, Marylise Léon, im Interview des Senders BFMTV.
Gewerkschaft: «Lohnerhöhung reicht nicht»

Die Generalsekretärin der Gewerkschaft CGT, Sophie Binet, hat die Ankündigung der Regierung, den Mindestlohn über die im Januar 2027 ohnehin anstehende Erhöhung weiter anheben zu wollen, gelobt. Jedoch sei es nicht mit einer zusätzlichen Erhöhung um 0.5 oder 0.6 Prozent getan. «Frankreich ist das europäische Land, in dem der Mindestlohn in den letzten zehn Jahren am wenigsten gestiegen ist.»
Der Mindestlohn pro Stunde liegt in Frankreich derzeit bei 12.31 Euro brutto. Ein zum Mindestlohn Beschäftigter in Frankreich kommt bei einer 35-Stunden-Woche auf rund 1.867 Euro brutto.

items.titel: Saudi coalition intercepts missile fired towards Medina
items.anriss: Interception comes after Saudi civil defence agency warned of potential danger near the strategic port of Yanbu.

absaetze.t: Interception comes after Saudi civil defence agency warned of potential danger near the strategic port of Yanbu.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis has said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Iran-aligned armed group towards the Medina region, home to one of Islam’s holiest cities.
The announcement on Thursday came just minutes after Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency warned of potential danger in the area near the strategic port of Yanbu.
“Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region,” coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a post on X.

The Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), have rejected any suggestion they were targeting the city, saying such accusations were a “blatant and grave falsehood”.
Houthi Military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X that “our operations target only oil facilities and military bases” and called the allegation a lie.
Among their attacks on airports, energy infrastructure and military sites, the Houthis have targeted the port of Yanbu on several occasions in recent months.
“A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in Yanbu Governorate to alert of a potential danger,” read a statement published by the agency online.
The agency later announced that the threat had passed.
Yanbu is a ⁠⁠major oil export hub ⁠⁠and a ⁠⁠key ⁠⁠outlet for oil shipments ‌‌transported through the kingdom’s ‌‌East-West ‌‌pipeline.
The port and pipeline have played a key role since the outbreak of the United States-Israeli war on Iran in February, helping Riyadh ship crude and fuel to global markets.
Separately, Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces made gains in the Sanamat area in Taiz governorate, where fighting continues to rage.
Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said on Thursday that government forces carried out 1,298 “targeting operations” against the Houthis in the past 24 hours and “managed to gain control” of Sanamat.
The latest operations killed about 400 Houthi fighters and destroyed 132 vehicles, cars or heavy weapons placements, he said. Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims.
Yemeni government forces previously reclaimed Taiz’s Dhubab district and key positions near the critical Bab al-Mandeb strait.
Meanwhile, on the al-Jawf front, military engineering units continue to clear recaptured sites of mines and booby traps, al-Nazili added.
Late last month, the government said 16,100 Houthi operatives and commanders had been killed or wounded since October 5.
The Houthis have not confirmed a death toll and have in the meantime been firing missiles regularly towards Saudi Arabia, hitting multiple airports and disrupting air traffic over the kingdom.

Yazeed al-Jeddawy, a research manager at the Sana’a Center for Strategic Studies, told Al Jazeera that the course of the conflict increasingly appears to be moving towards a prolonged war of attrition as the government offensive has not shifted the balance of power over the past 30 days.
“The conflict is no longer driven solely by the dynamics inside Yemen; it is intertwined with the wider regional confrontation and the war involving Iran,” he added.

items.titel: Republicans have a ticking clock. What can they get done on defense?
items.anriss: Reconciliation, defense appropriations and the NDAA will all fight for attention as Congress considers the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

absaetze.t: WASHINGTON — Republicans are under the gun to pass defense funding during the lame duck session following a crippling loss in midterm elections, but first they’ll have to square off against emboldened Democrats seeking to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and curb the Iran war.

With only five legislative weeks remaining in the year, GOP leaders may make a last ditch effort to pass partyline reconciliation funding and a fiscal 2027 budget before Democrats take control of the House and Senate in January, experts said.
The big problem: Democrats may not be willing to come to the table.

“There’s zero chance of appropriations getting passed because that requires 60 votes in the Senate. Republicans do not have 60 votes in the Senate for any kind of appropriations bill,” said Todd Harrison, a defense analyst with the American Enterprise Institute. “Democrats have zero incentive to reach any kind of a deal on appropriations because now they’ve taken both chambers by substantial majorities.”
The Pentagon has requested funding for defense via three different vehicles:
A $1.15 trillion discretionary defense budget
A $350 billion mandatory funding request that would be funded through the partyline reconciliation process
A supplemental funding request that includes $67 billion for defense to recoup expenses associated with the Iran war

Another key item on the to-do list: The FY27 National Defense Authorization Act, an annual bill that does not provide funding, but contains defense policy changes ranging from troop pay raises to defense acquisition reform.
None of the three funding vehicles have been approved by Congress, and the path toward passage has become much more complicated as a result of the landslide Democrat wins, experts said.

In a note to investors on Wednesday, TD Cowen analyst Roman Schweizer said that a sweeping Democratic takeover of the House and Senate is the “toughest” scenario for defense spending. The lame duck period is “now critical” as the “last shot at [reconciliation],” with both the NDAA and defense appropriations likely delayed until early 2027.

VJ Sahi, partner and senior vice president at Clark Street Associates, told Breaking Defense that in the early weeks of the lame duck, Republicans could view a reconciliation bill “as the last train leaving the station” and could push a mandatory funding package forward that would at least cover the Iran war costs.
But even without needing Democrat votes, Republican leadership will face both old and new challenges in getting partyline support for reconciliation, defense analysts said.

The House passed a budget resolution in July that would start the reconciliation process, with $60 billion for defense. But Senate Majority Leader John Thune repeatedly refused to bring it up for a vote in the upper chamber, stating that there weren’t enough Republican votes to pass the measure.

After the midterms, Republican leadership will have to contend with the same concerns from fiscal hawks about how reconciliation funding will be paid for. And if Republicans departing Congress at the end of the year decide not to show up for the lame duck session, they might not have the numbers to even get a simple majority, Harrison said.
“I think the most likely case is it doesn’t go anywhere, it doesn’t even get a vote,” Harrison said.

A day after the election, Capital Alpha Partners analyst Byron Callan reduced his prediction that further defense reconciliation will pass Congress from 15 percent to 10 percent. He was similarly sanguine about the chances of passing FY27 appropriations, projecting a 50 percent chance of a government shutdown after the current continuing resolution (CR) expires on Dec. 11.

“The magnitude of Democratic gains in the House and Senate from the midterm elections suggests that nothing will get done by Congress for defense legislation in Nov.-Dec,” Callan wrote in a note to investors Wednesday.

If budget negotiations stall until January, when the 120th Congress is sworn in, Democrats could potentially boost funds for nondefense priorities while reining in defense spending to be well below the $1.5 trillion level the Trump administration was angling for in FY27.
Washington Rep. Adam Smith, who will probably take the gavel as the House Armed Services Committee chairman, signaled in a letter Wednesday that he would support a more restrained defense budget.

“We must push for the development of a more realistic and sustainable approach to our national security — one that does not require a defense budget in excess of $1 trillion or one paid for with draconian cuts to critical domestic programs,” Smith wrote.

Connecticut Rep. Rosa DeLauro — House Appropriations Committee’s top Democrat and likely chairwoman come January — did not explicitly call for lower defense spending in a letter where she laid out her priorities. However, she set up a potential fight with the Office of Management and Budget over how previous reconciliation dollars sent to the Defense Department were spent.

“We must claw back billions of dollars Republicans unilaterally provided to Border Patrol, ICE, and the Pentagon through budget reconciliation in an end run outside of the Appropriations Committee,” she stated.

With reconciliation unlikely and a probable defense topline of roughly $1.1 trillion for FY27, the Pentagon will need to make hard choices in terms of what items should be transferred from the mandatory request to the discretionary budget — and what items will be cut in order to free up those dollars.

“Missile defense interceptor replenishment will remain a priority, but it is highly unlikely that all of the $47 billion in mandatory [request] is funded in discretionary,” Callan wrote in a note to investors. The Pentagon is also unlikely to get all of the F-35s included in the mandatory request added to the baseline appropriations bill, and the funding for its Drone Dominance effort could get shaved down to a “fraction” of its $53.6 billion request, he added.
Harrison and Callan agreed that in an environment where Democrats control the defense budget, the Trump-class battleship won’t receive funding.

Golden Dome — another signature program of the Trump administration — may survive in parts, but it suffers from a lack of Democrat support and the fact that the vast majority of its funding for FY27 was supposed to be paid for by reconciliation, Harrison said.
“If you dissect it and look at the different parts of Golden Dome, I think there are many parts that would enjoy bipartisan support,” he said.

However, “the Golden Dome Caucus on the Hill never included a single Democrat. Democrats have not been getting the briefings on it that Republicans have, so there’s just not buy-in for the program,” he added.

And the longer budget negotiations extend, the more complicated they could become. If the debt ceiling isn’t addressed by a GOP-led reconciliation bill, and FY27 budget talks stretch until spring, those negotiations could be combined, Schweizer said in a note today.

“It’s a tale as old as time: build a mega policy cliff” that combines government funding and a debt ceiling raise, Schweizer said. “If that happens, we would expect a 2-year discretionary spending deal combined with a debt ceiling raise.”
The Hegseth Question

One looming question hanging over the lame duck is the fate of Hegseth, who has come into the crosshairs of lawmakers blaming him for the Iran war — widely seen as a key reason why the GOP lost the midterms.
Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., reiterated on Wednesday that he will bring articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when Congress returns to Washington next week.
“There is one contingency in which I won’t reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns,” he said in a post on X.
Hegseth could have an obvious exit strategy. Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected as Tennessee’s governor in the midterms, could appoint Hegseth to fill her Senate seat when she leaves Washington.
But if that’s the plan, it would be best for Hegseth to resign quickly, Harrison said.

“If Hegseth resigns now in the lame duck session, the Senate, while it’s still under Republican control, has time to confirm a new SECDEF,” he said. “If that falls to the next Senate, with a 54 or 55 seat majority with Democrats, Trump is going to have a hard time getting anyone confirmed.”
Massie told Fox News that he intends to force a vote on Hegseth’s impeachment by filing a privileged resolution, which would compel a House vote within two days.

One lobbyist who spoke to Breaking Defense said Vice President JD Vance’s post on X blaming the Iran war for the GOP loss in the midterms will provide some Republican lawmakers the political top cover needed to vote for Hegseth’s impeachment.

For a Republican who views JD Vance as the future of the party, “a vote to impeach Hegseth over Iran … [is] a political vote I’m willing to take,” the lobbyist said. “If you have members that are [thinking], ‘This could be one of the final votes that I cast as a member of Congress. This is the legacy that I’m leaving, and Iran is obviously deeply unpopular’… I feel like that is a very politically safe vote for a lot of folks to take.”
Earlier today, Hegseth published a defiant video message on X where he called the Iran war a “a courageous and historic effort” and referenced the potential impeachment vote directly.

“A disgruntled, defeated congressman, along with all his Democrat allies, has also dropped sham articles of impeachment against yours truly, just like they tried against President Trump twice,” he said. “It’s all about the politics of personal destruction. Didn’t work against President Trump, and it won’t work with me.”
Since the election, Trump has repeatedly denied news reports that he was considering replacing Hegseth, telling reporters on Wednesday that Hegseth “is doing a very good job.”
Asked whether he wanted Hegseth to be appointed to fill Blackburn’s senatorial seat, Trump said that Hegseth “would be very popular if he did that, but I haven’t heard that at all.”
Harrison said he didn’t buy that explanation.
“When your boss starts saying you’d be great at a different job, that’s a sign,” he said.
Democrats Set Sights On Iran War, Oversight

Democrats have made clear that investigating the Trump administration will be a major legislative goal, with lawmakers already beginning to lay out their oversight priorities during the lame duck session.

In September, Rep. Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, sent a letter to the National Defense Industrial Association informing the trade group of a“likely” investigation into corporate donations to President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom project, which include defense contractors like Lockheed Martin.

Some Democrats, including Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Colorado Rep. Jason Crow, have previously raised concerns about Pentagon contracts being awarded to companies with ties to the Trump brothers.
“I think it will be an issue for defense companies, especially those that have been invested in by the president’s family,” the lobbyist said.

In the Wednesday letter outlining Democrat priorities for HASC, Smith wrote that he would support reestablishing an oversight subcommittee, which could investigate waste, fraud and abuse by defense contractors as well as current operations.

“The list of potential oversight topics is long, but the illegal war against Iran is top of mind for me and the American people. So too are sweetheart deals and favoritism to certain entities and individuals,” Smith stated.

“The list continues with the unauthorized military strikes in the Caribbean and Latin America, the deployment of the military to U.S. cities, and the blatant and corrosive politicization of our Armed Forces and purging of the ranks based on loyalty and ideology are high on the list,” he added.

items.titel: China’s Military Helicopters: A Guide
items.anriss: China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) operates an increasingly diverse fleet of helicopters spanning everything from basic pilot training and battlefield transport to airborne early warning, anti-submarine warfare, and dedicated attack …

absaetze.t: China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) operates an increasingly diverse fleet of helicopters spanning everything from basic pilot training and battlefield transport to airborne early warning, anti-submarine warfare, and dedicated attack missions.

The force reflects decades of development, often beginning with helicopters acquired from France and later produced under license, before transitioning to increasingly indigenous designs. The result is a mix of older aircraft that have undergone extensive modernization and newer platforms designed around the requirements of China’s expanding military, including its growing carrier and amphibious assault fleets.

The Z-8 family, originally derived from the Cold War-era French Super Frelon, is a particularly good example of this evolution. It has spawned a wide range of specialized variants, including search and rescue, transport, electronic warfare, and airborne command post helicopters. Meanwhile, the Z-20 — frequently alluded to as a Sikorsky S-70/H-60 clone — has emerged as a modern medium-lift platform with land-based, naval, and assault variants, while the Z-10 and newer Z-21 represent China’s growing emphasis on dedicated attack helicopters.
This guide examines the principal helicopter types operated by the PLA, their development, and the roles they are expected to perform.
At the same time, it should be noted that, as it now stands, the PLA remains heavily reliant on foreign-sourced helicopters for a wide variety of applications.

Russian-built helicopters give the PLA a mix of transport and specialized naval capabilities. The Mi-17/171 Hip family supports troop and cargo movement, search and rescue, special operations, and select high-altitude or mission-specific roles. At sea, the Ka-28 Helix provides anti-submarine warfare, while the Ka-31’s radar supports airborne fleet surveillance. These aircraft remain in service where their established capabilities continue to meet operational needs. However, they are increasingly supplemented by Chinese designs, including certain designs that have been tailored to provide direct replacements.
Utility, Training, and Light Helicopters

The HC-120 is a light utility helicopter derived from the EC120, a design co-developed by China, France, and Singapore during the 1990s. The type entered service with PLA Army Aviation in 2005, providing a modern platform for primary helicopter training and replacing the aging SA316 Alouette III in that role.

The HC-120 is powered by a single Turbomeca Arrius 2F turboshaft engine. Its introduction represented an important step in modernizing the Army Aviation training fleet, giving pilots experience with a more contemporary helicopter before transitioning to larger operational types.

The Z-11 is a light utility helicopter developed by Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation (CHAIC) and the 602 Research Institute. The design is based on the French AS350BA Écureuil, examples of which were acquired for Army Aviation.
Deliveries of the Z-11 to Army Aviation began in 1998. The helicopter is powered by a single WZ-8D turboshaft engine and is primarily used for training, liaison, and other light utility duties.

A scout and armed reconnaissance derivative, designated as the Z-11WB, was developed with a nose-mounted electro-optical (EO) turret and external weapon pylons capable of carrying rockets, missiles, and gun pods. Its operational status remains unclear, although it provided the basis for the unarmed Z-11A training helicopter used by the Army Aviation Academy.
The Z-8 Family: From French Origins To A Modern Helicopter Lineage
Z-8J

The Z-8 was developed from the French SA321Ja Super Frelon, 13 examples of which China purchased during the late 1970s. Changhe Aircraft Industries Corporation subsequently developed an indigenous version during the 1980s.

Powered by three WZ-6 turboshaft engines, the original Z-8 became the foundation for a broad family of helicopters serving the PLA Navy (PLAN), Army Aviation, and People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF).

The Z-8J is the naval transport variant, with a boat-like hull. For anti-submarine warfare (ASW) missions, the helicopter can be equipped with a surface-search radar, a French HS-12 dipping sonar, and Whitehead A244S or ET52 torpedoes.
Several specialized derivatives were developed from the Z-8J:

Z-8S: A naval search and rescue (SAR) version with upgraded avionics, a searchlight, a forward-looking infrared (FLIR) turret, and a rescue hoist. Most Z-8Js have reportedly been upgraded to this configuration.
Z-8JH: A medical evacuation and SAR variant.
The Z-8J and Z-8JH have both been used aboard Chinese aircraft carriers, providing transport and support capabilities for embarked naval forces.
Z-8C

The Z-8C represents a substantially improved successor to the original naval Z-8J series. The helicopter was first reported in 2016 and incorporates a number of changes intended to improve its performance and operational versatility.

The most visible differences include a redesigned nose with a chin-mounted weather radar, a FLIR turret, and a pilot night-vision system (PNVS) mounted above the cockpit. A searchlight is also fitted, while the longer engine compartment accommodates the WZ-6C turboshaft engine.
The Z-8C is operated by the PLA Marine Corps, while the Z-8CJ serves as a training variant with the Naval Aviation University.
The helicopter has become a principal transport platform for the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, supporting the movement of troops and equipment between ships and shore.
Z-8K/KA

The PLAAF introduced the Z-8K in 2007 as a dedicated search-and-rescue helicopter. The related Z-8KA is configured for combat search and rescue (CSAR), including the recovery of personnel from hostile or contested environments.

Both versions feature a FLIR turret, searchlight, radar-warning receiver (RWR), chaff and flare dispensers, and a rescue hoist. Some aircraft are also equipped with small terrain-following radars beneath the nose to support low-level operations.
Selected helicopters have received satellite communications (SATCOM) antennas on top of the tail boom, improving their communications capabilities over longer distances.
A further derivative, the Z-8KH, was developed for the PLAAF garrison stationed in Hong Kong. This version is distinguished by chaff and flare dispensers integrated into its flotation equipment.
Z-8B
The Z-8B entered service with PLA Army Aviation in 2011 as an improved transport helicopter. It shares several characteristics with the Z-8KH but lacks the latter’s flotation equipment.

The Z-8B incorporates a glass cockpit and has become a major component of the Army Aviation transport fleet. Some aircraft have subsequently had flotation equipment reinstalled, reflecting the type’s continuing evolution.

An optional auxiliary fuel tank can be installed inside the cabin to extend its range. Other upgrades have included SATCOM antennas on the tail boom and, on some aircraft, WZ-6C engines, an EO turret, and a terrain-following radar beneath the nose.

A specialized operations variant has also been identified. These helicopters incorporate RWR, laser-warning receivers (LWR), and missile-approach warning system (MAWS) sensors, alongside flare dispensers and ceramic armor protection.
Z-8G

Lacking the boat-like hull of the Z-8B, the Z-8G is expected to replace that type in Army Aviation service. The helicopter was evaluated from 2014 and was specifically optimized for operations at high altitudes, including in Tibet.

Unlike earlier Z-8 variants, the initial Z-8G configuration uses imported Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6B-67A turboshaft engines. Its redesigned nose is longer and more aerodynamically efficient, while the glass cockpit and terrain-following radar support operations in demanding environments.
The helicopter also incorporates SATCOM and BeiDou/GPS antennas to improve communications and navigation during long-range missions.

Some Z-8Gs have been equipped for special operations, with combinations of MAWS, RWR, and LWR sensors mounted on the rear fuselage and sponsons, together with chaff and flare dispensers. Armor plates beneath the cockpit windows provide additional protection, and some aircraft carry a 12.7mm machine gun inside a cabin doorway.
Several specialized variants have also been identified:
A battlefield electronic-warfare helicopter featuring large cylindrical antennas mounted on both sides of the mid-fuselage.
Another electronic warfare configuration reportedly uses rectangular plate antenna arrays mounted on both sides of the rear fuselage.
An airborne command-post variant featuring a retractable synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) surveillance system inside the rear fuselage, alongside additional electronic-support-measures (ESM) antennas.
Some Z-8Gs may also have adopted the indigenous WZ-6C engine.
Z-8L

The Z-8L is a wide-body development of the Z-8G that first flew in 2017. Its most prominent feature is a pair of large sponsons mounted along the sides of the fuselage, providing additional space for fuel tanks and other equipment.

The wider fuselage also increases internal volume, allowing the helicopter to carry more cargo and equipment. Relocating the internal fuel tanks beneath the cabin floor has further increased usable cabin space.

Some aircraft have been observed with RWR and MAWS sensors on both sides of the forward fuselage, a roof-mounted FLIR turret, and a terrain-following radar beneath the nose. Additional defensive equipment, including LWR and RWR sensors and chaff/flare dispensers, can be installed on the sponsons.
A SATCOM antenna is mounted on top of the tail boom. The original PT6B-67A engines are reportedly being replaced by the more powerful indigenous WZ-7 turboshaft.
The Z-8L provides the Army with a larger and more capable transport helicopter suited to demanding operating environments and specialized missions.
Z-8D

The Z-8D is a shipborne derivative of the Z-8L that first appeared in 2023. It combines the wide-body configuration with an extensive self-defense suite intended to improve survivability during operations over water.
The helicopter features RWR, LWR, and MAWS sensors, along with chaff and flare dispensers. Four inflatable flotation units provide emergency protection in the event of a forced landing at sea.

Power is supplied by either WZ-6C or the newer WZ-7 turboshaft engines. Engine air particle separators (EAPS) are installed ahead of the engine inlets to reduce the risk of damage from airborne debris.
The Z-8D is expected to operate from China’s Type 075 amphibious assault ships and the larger Type 076 amphibious assault ship.
The Z-18 Series: Naval Utility, Early Warning, and ASW Helicopters
Z-18Y

Named White Heron, the Z-18Y was developed by the 602 Research Institute and Changhe as a new medium-lift shipborne transport helicopter. It is derived from the AC313 but incorporates a redesigned fuselage and a number of changes intended to improve its naval suitability.

The helicopter uses imported PT6B-67A turboshaft engines and provides greater internal volume and payload capacity than the earlier Z-8. Improved performance in hot-and-high conditions is another important feature.

The Z-18Y incorporates a nose-mounted weather radar and an FLIR/TV turret, along with additional communication and navigation antennas beneath the fuselage. A SATCOM antenna is installed on top of the tail boom.

Folding main and tail rotor blades allow the helicopter to be stored more efficiently aboard ships. The Z-18Y is primarily used for carrier onboard delivery (COD) missions, transporting personnel and supplies between ships and shore.
It has also provided the basis for several specialized naval derivatives.
Z-18J
Named Bat, the Z-18J is an airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) helicopter developed from the Z-18Y.

items.titel: It’s Time to Talk About Classism in the Art World
items.anriss: For something that determines so much — about the art we make, the art we get to see or not, the art that may never be made at all — the issue of class is rarely discussed in the art world. Breaking the silence, artist and writer Mark …

absaetze.t: In his memoiristic new book, photographer Mark Alice Durant weaves his personal experiences into a larger rebuke of the economic inequality that governs the art world.
November 5, 2026 — 3 min read

For something that determines so much — about the art we make, the art we get to see or not, the art that may never be made at all — the issue of class is rarely discussed in the art world. Breaking the silence, artist and writer Mark Alice Durant speaks up in his memoir-cum-rebuke, Confessions of a Working Class Artist (2026). It reads both like a Künstlerroman and an updated version of the seminal guide for the aspiring artist, Rainer Maria Rilke’s Letters to a Young Poet (1929), for our dystopian neo-Gilded Age.

For Durant, also the author of the moving photographic memoir Summer of the White Fox, and After (2024) and publisher at Saint Lucy Books, which released both titles, choosing to become an artist was an act of self-exile. He writes that he psychically uprooted himself from the working-class precincts of Boston where he grew up as well as from his extended family, with the exception of his mother, unusually open-minded and supportive of her son. Perhaps she saw herself in his youthful gift of a framed reproduction of Jules Breton’s 1884 painting of a field worker, “The Song of the Lark.” After deciding on this path, Durant writes, “I could never return home on some level.”

items.titel: Ex-husband of Brent Sikkema sentenced to life in prison over murder-for-hire killing
items.anriss: Daniel Sikkema, who was married to Brent Sikkema for 15 years, had been convicted of orchestrating his grisly 2024 murder

absaetze.t: The former husband of the late New York art dealer Brent Sikkema, Daniel Sikkema, aged 56, has been sentenced to life imprisonment for organising Sikkema’s murder in 2024. A federal court in Manhattan handed down the sentence on Wednesday (4 November).

In May 2026, after a two-week trial, Daniel Sikkema was convicted on charges of murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit murder in a foreign country. In addition to life imprisonment, he was sentenced to five years of supervised release.

Brent Sikkema, who was aged 75 at the time of his murder, was found stabbed to death at his home in the Jardim Botânico neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on 15 January 2024. According to prosecutors, Daniel Sikkema began planning the murder in 2023 in the midst of his divorce from the dealer, with whom he had been married for around 15 years and shared a son.

As the couple’s divorce proceedings became more acrimonious, Daniel Sikkema, who holds dual US and Cuban citizenship, recruited the Cuban national, Alejandro Triana Prevez, as the hitman. On the night of the murder, Prevez entered the late Sikkema’s residence and stabbed him 18 times. Prevez subsequently received $5,000 from Daniel Sikkema and was promised further payments.

Prosecutors said Daniel Sikkema made 11 payments to Prevez and Prevez’s partner in Cuba, using the identities of unwitting friends, employees and family members to conceal the transactions. Prevez was arrested by Brazilian authorities four days after the murder at a gas station on the side of the highway in the state of Minas Gerais, around 600 miles from Rio de Janeiro. He had stolen cash and jewellery in his possession. His case is being handled separately by a Brazilian court.

Brent Sikkema was born in 1948 in Morrison, Illinois, and studied at the San Francisco Art Institute before beginning his career. In the early 1990s, he founded Wooster Gardens in SoHo, moving the gallery to Chelsea in 1999. The business became Sikkema Jenkins & Co in 2003 following the involvement of Michael Jenkins and Meg Malloy.

The gallery is now known as Sikkema Malloy Jenkins and continues to operate in Chelsea. It has championed the work of artists including Kara Walker, Vik Muniz, Sheila Hicks, Jeffrey Gibson and Arturo Herrera. A representative for Sikkema Malloy Jenkins told The Art Newspaper that the gallery will not be providing any statement regarding the conviction or sentencing.

items.titel: SWA implements modular "toolkit" for a more walkable Houston
items.anriss: Landscape architecture studio SWA has designed a modular system including petal-shaped shade structures, outdoor lighting and planting beds that can be deployed around the city in an effort to create a more comfortable streetscape in …

absaetze.t: Landscape architecture studio SWA has designed a modular system including petal-shaped shade structures, outdoor lighting and planting beds that can be deployed around the city in an effort to create a more comfortable streetscape in Houston, Texas, USA.
The Cool & Connected Corridors project seeks to retrofit the streets of Houston with cooling infrastructure to create a more walkable pedestrian experience.
The project is part of the city’s wider Public Realm Action Plan initiative aimed at making the urban streetscape “more delightful, comfortable and easy”, according to the city.

The network of architectural elements is designed to be integrated into varying, pre-existing sidewalk conditions, according to the team, and have been installed along a 15-block stretch of the city’s Texas Avenue as Phase 1 of the Public Realm Action Plan roll-out.

“Cool & Connected Corridors is a blueprint for taking action here and now, showing how cities can layer social, economic, and environmental benefits in a cost-efficient way,” said SWA principal Natalia Beard.

The “easily replicable toolkit” includes three main components – a lighting system aimed at improving visibility and safety at night, modular planting beds and mesh cooling pavilions designed by architecture studio Höweler + Yoon.
The petal-shaped pavilions are made of bead-blasted stainless steel, with mesh membranes in gradients of blue, green and purple.
They stretch up overhead, providing shade on street corners during the day, and integrated lighting illuminates them at night.
According to the team, they were designed to be installed as a single unit, or clustered together to form “bouquets”.
“Together, they create a sequence of shaded landmarks that help orient pedestrians from block to block,” said Höweler + Yoon co-founder Meejin Yoon.
The integrated lighting designed for the system is globe- and line-form lighting that drops down from the tree canopy.
According to the team, it was informed by a lighting study performed by the city in 2023, which identified a master plan for illuminating the nightime streetscape.
Other elements in the Cool & Connected Corridors system include wayfinding, replacement trees and a careful selection of drought-tolerant and pollinator-supportive plants throughout the planters.
The system along Texas Avenue was installed in the city ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Since its installation, “thermal infrared readings of ground surfaces beneath the shade structures show an average temperature reduction of 10°F (5°C), with reductions of up to 30°F (16°C) in some locations”, said SWA.
Next, the city plans to install the system along the remaining portion of Texas Avenue and along other strips of the downtown area including McKinney Street and Preston Street.
Another recent urbanism project aimed at improving walkability is the pedestrianisation of Oxford Street in London.
Elsewhere in Houston, STG recently released renders of a twisting skyscraper, while the city is also set to receive projects by OMA and Theaster Gates.

items.titel: Perrier-Jouët and Iris van Herpen partnership celebrates “biological processes that shape life”
items.anriss: Champagne house Perrier-Jouët has unveiled a creative collection with designer Iris van Herpen that draws on art nouveau design, soundscapes and the “invisible forces that shape the natural world”.

absaetze.t: Champagne house Perrier-Jouët has unveiled a creative collection with designer Iris van Herpen that draws on art nouveau design, soundscapes and the “invisible forces that shape the natural world”.
As part of the partnership, Van Herpen created Symphonic Bloom, a sculptural piece crafted from silk and recycled 22-carat gold.

The collectable sculpture was designed to delicately twirl up the neck of a Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque 1988 jeroboam champagne bottle. According to Van Herpen, it reflects “the unseen” and represents hidden entities, such as sound and energy frequencies.

During the piece’s creation, the designer recorded soundscapes of Perrier-Jouët’s champagne vineyards, documenting acoustic patterns via cymatics – a technology that makes sound waves visible via sand or water. The sculpture’s patterns are based on such vibrations.
“In nature, there is a silent yet ever-present dance of frequencies, rhythms, and biological processes that continuously shape life,” Van Herpen explained.
“The world is not only visual but vibrational – woven together by invisible forces that connect all living things,” the designer added.
The nature-informed element of the sculpture’s craft connects to Perrier-Jouët’s experimental regenerative viticulture programme, which aims to sustainably restore soil health across its vineyards.
Since 2021, the initiative has been successfully undertaken across 40 per cent of its sites.
This mirrors Van Herpen’s sustainability ethos, with the designer incorporating recycled materials into her designs and using techniques to minimise waste as much as possible.
In keeping with its multidisciplinary theme, Symphonic Bloom was also created to reflect the layered flavours of Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque cuvées and how they develop with time.
Alongside the sculpture, Van Herpen also produced Symphonic Life, a collectable edition of a Perrier-Jouët Belle Époque 1999 magnum, adorned in the botanical motifs seen in Symphonic Bloom.

Completing the set of collaborative cuvees is a bespoke version of Perrier-Jouët Belle Epoque 2018 that comes with a reimagined bottle and gift box, made in collaboration with cellar master Séverine Frerson.

“Inspired by the designer’s interplay of materials including metal, wood, silk and velvet, the cuvée reveals notes of white flowers, poached pear and grapefruit, lifted by a delicate touch of white pepper and a fine, silky finish,” said Séverine of Perrier-Jouët Belle Epoque 2018.
Perrier-Jouët explained that the collaboration with Van Herpen is built on a shared philosophy that spotlights and advocates for nature as a source of “inspiration, creation and transformation”.

“Treating nature as a collaborator, Iris van Herpen is one of fashion’s most forward-thinking designers, with a practice that reveals the invisible beauty of living systems, translating organic forces, micro-rhythms and subterranean life into visible form,” said Axelle de Buffevant, creative director of Perrier-Jouët.
De Buffévent explained that the shared mindset also mirrors its connections with the art nouveau movement, with which it has a long-standing cultural and artistic affinity.

The design movement’s reference was also interpreted by Van Herpen across the whole collaboration, where the movements of American dancer Loïe Fuller were also used as a source of inspiration across the project.
Fuller’s movements were used in art nouveau lamp design by French sculptor Raoul Larche, which is part of Perrier-Jouët’s extensive French art nouveau collection at Maison Belle Époque in Épernay.
The creations were presented on 21 October for Perrier-Jouët’s Banquet of Nature at The Peninsula Paris, which combined champagne, art and gastronomy into an interactive sensory gathering.
The project will continue its international journey in Miami, Florida, for the city’s design week in December 2026, of which the brand has a longstanding history.
“For many years, Perrier-Jouët and Design Miami have shared a commitment to creativity, craftsmanship and contemporary culture,” the brand said.
Perrier-Jouët is a partner of the fair and last year launched its Design for Nature Award, of which Van Herpen was the first recipient.
This year, during Design Miami, a final collaborative sculptural piece will be revealed, created by Van Herpen as the winner of the award.
To learn more about the collaboration, visit Perrier-Jouët’s website.
